uncited: **Inputs:** A list of $N_{total}$ Gaussian splats, where each splat contains position ($\mathbf{p}$), scale ($\mathbf{s}$), rotation ($\mathbf{q}$), spherical harmonic coefficients ($\mathbf{c}$), and opacity ($\alpha$).
**Outputs:** A set of compressed GPU textures and metadata (chunk min/max values) allowing reconstruction of splat parameters.
**Chunk Metadata:** For each chunk, store the minimum and maximum values for every data field (position, scale, color, SH) in full Float32 precision.
**Texture Layout:** Textures are organized such that one texel represents one splat.
Within a chunk of $N=256$ splats, the data is arranged in a $16 \times 16$ square layout.
Sort the splats in the data array based on their 3D positions using 3D Morton order.
This ensures that spatially nearby splats are adjacent in the array.
Group the reordered splats into contiguous chunks of size $N=256$.
For each chunk, compute the global minimum and maximum values for all data fields across all splats in that chunk using full Float32 precision.
*Rotation Encoding:* Quaternions are encoded using the "smallest three" format.
Store the three smallest components of the quaternion and the index of the largest component.
Reorder the texture data within each chunk into a $16 \times 16$ square layout using 2D Morton order.
Encode the normalized splat data into GPU textures.
Select a texture format based on the desired quality/compression trade-off.
*   **Compression Quality:** Storing data in $256 \times 1$ stripes causes poor compression quality with BCn formats because the compression is block-based ($4 \times 4$ texels).
*   **Large Chunk Bounds:** If Morton curve flips cause large chunk bounds, variance within the chunk increases, reducing normalization efficiency.
*   **Strengths:** Significant reduction in model size (up to ~19x) with acceptable quality loss at higher compression levels.
Leverages existing GPU texture hardware for decompression.
Lower quality presets (Very Low) may introduce visible artifacts.
It addresses the large storage footprint of 3D Gaussian Splatting models, which typically store parameters in full Float32 precision.
